quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is legally intoxicated.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: In most places, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while intoxicated.

questions.question: Riding directly alongside another vehicle is dangerous because:

options.text: You may have a hard time reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may change lanes into you without seeing you. Also, the vehicle will block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If you brake while turning in a curve:

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but be very careful. When you lean the motorcycle to turn, some tire grip is used for turning. This means less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: At a blind intersection with a stop sign, riders should:

options.text: Stop at the sign, then drive through the intersection.
Ignore the sign and move forward to see better.
Stop at the sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sign, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, stop where the sign indicates. Then move forward slowly and stop again near the crossroad. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself as visible as possible. Wear bright-colored clothes when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Your position in the lane should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Give you a good view of the scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide what you plan to do from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: The right lane position improves safety in many ways. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps other drivers see you, helps you avoid hazards, protects you from wind blasts, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle, you should ride in the left part of your lane because:

options.text: It improves what you can see.
It reduces what you can see.
It makes it hard to see past the vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It improves what you can see.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. This improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely so the bike can move.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use high throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it does not cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: On rough surfaces, hold the handgrips firmly. This keeps you in control of your motorcycle's direction.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: In a turn, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see better and be seen by others.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It keeps other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at a motorcycle and still do not notice it. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or nerves can make you drowsy and hurt your riding ability. Before riding, know how any medication affects your body.

questions.question: Which of the following best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: The front brake supplies how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle may weave on rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and go straight at a steady speed. Weaving to compensate will only make it worse.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either the front or rear brake, but not both.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider discourage other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding in the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to leave less space on each side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You can go up to 10 mph over the speed limit to complete the pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the shoulder if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Pass only where it is safe and legal. Stay within the speed limit and only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, it is best to:

options.text: Let one rider finish passing before the next rider starts to pass.
Have several riders pass the other vehicle at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal that no other motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider finish passing before the next rider starts to pass.
questions.explanation: In a group, riders should pass one at a time. Each rider should complete their pass and return to the group before the next rider begins.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals 4 drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are not familiar with them, you should practice using them because:

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make things look farther away than they really are.
Unlike flat mirrors, they make things look closer than they really are.
It can be hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unlike flat mirrors, they make things look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view behind you than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Practice using them if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is located near the right footrest on a motorcycle.

questions.question: Before riding, check all of the following except:

options.text: The condition of your tire sidewalls.

questions.correctAnswerText: How reflective your tires are.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tire pressure, tire tread, and the overall condition of your tire sidewalls and surfaces. You do not need to check how reflective your tires are.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others, signal your intentions, keep safe distance, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and stay ready to react to changes.

questions.question: Convex mirrors make cars look:
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wider view than flat mirrors, but they make objects look farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best way to stay close while keeping safe distance is to ride:
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving everyone enough space. Use single-file when turning or entering highways. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen with:

options.text: Those who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often with inexperienced, beginning riders who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: To swerve, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, push on the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To turn left, push the left handgrip, then the right to straighten out. To turn right, push the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes occur on short trips of less than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts.
